study.question: Does removing the event-count prior of each observed behavior improve target-conditioned, field-aligned history retrieval, beyond the generic effect of redistributing attention weights?
study.hypothesis: Observation: static/pooled/DIN validation AUCs are 0.605004/0.610226/0.613362. The earlier target-directional gate reached only 0.611415, below DIN, despite beating its scalar/context controls; it did not establish external architecture transfer. Event-level field-aligned target retrieval subsequently reached 0.615335 versus 0.614609 consensus and 0.611024 context-separate. Exact aligned replay reproduced AUC and Logloss; this is a reproducibility check, not an independent seed. Arithmetic whole-event pooling (0.614920), crossed routing (0.613833), and whole-event context retrieval (0.610908) failed to improve the incumbent. Preserve aligned values rather than extend that unsuccessful coupling branch. An unresolved structural limitation is that all events compete in one softmax: a behavior with n events receives n times the prior mass at equal scores. Existing presence slices show multi-behavior histories are available (2,111,110 cart-present, 1,179,004 favorite-present and 1,888,339 buy-present validation impressions out of 3,234,051), but do NOT establish per-impression count imbalance or harmful crowding. Proposed mechanism hypothesis: conditional on this supplied history, removing the n_a prior allows sparse behavior evidence to contribute according to average target relevance instead of multiplicity. Record counts and masses to check whether the proposed bottleneck is active. This is a provisional local hypothesis, not controlled support or a novelty claim.

nearest_work.difference: DIN already supplies target-conditioned local activation and weighted history pooling. Its primary text explicitly abandons softmax to preserve intensity; the host DIN-style reference instead uses softmax. We inherit the local reference scorer, not exact DIN. Proposed action-count correction changes the base measure of the existing normalized read; output norm remains target-independent. No DIN reproduction or first-use claim.

The source already retrieves each of four behavior domains with item-field queries and generates/refines probes using attention and multiple views. Our count-prior intervention is motivated by the local softmax denominator, not a claim that behavior separation or field-to-history retrieval is new. It adds no probes, tokenization views, domain modules, capacity or sequence bridge. Equivalent to within-action softmax followed by a relevance-based domain mixture using log-mean-exp scores, rather than explicit learned domain queries. Broader hierarchical-attention priority remains unverified.

Candidate-aware multi-domain retrieval and explicit boundary relevance are prior art. No bus fusion, highway, SwiGLU gate, temporal interleaving, auxiliary head or mutual learning is adopted. Our earlier gating branch lost to DIN; current changes cannot be credited to UniDot.

inherited_components: Field-specific category/brand embeddings shared with current-ad features; action and age embeddings
Two target-conditioned DIN-style relation evaluations with a shared scorer and independent softmaxes
Aligned category and brand values, mean attention for action/age values
Target-independent masked-mean reference norm and finite empty-history fallback
Unchanged static feature concatenation, MLP dimensions, optimizer, loss and frozen training protocol
study.proposed_difference: For each field f and valid event i, compute n_a from valid supplied history_type values and w_fi = softmax_i(s_fi - log(n_{a_i})). At equal scores, each present action receives equal total mass; when scores differ its mass is proportional to mean_i_in_action exp(s_fi), so action importance remains target-conditioned rather than forced uniform. This is equivalent to within-action normalized reads with log-mean-exp action logits. Action counts are computed only within the supplied truncated causal prefix, never full inaccessible histories. A half-cycle rotation of packed valid action labels provides a deterministic count-histogram-matched correction control; actual type embeddings, values, ages, event order and masks are unchanged. All four standalone modules have identical parameters, construction order and count bookkeeping; CONFIG changes only query source and chosen prior (action, shifted, none). No package installation, training, external access, global state, labels or filesystem operations in model code.
predictions: Predeclared primary contrast: action_target exceeds global_target full-population validation ROC-AUC; secondary Logloss must be reported even if it disagrees. No numerical minimum improvement or statistical significance is assumed from a single seed.

Mechanism contrast: action_target exceeds shifted_target; otherwise generic event reweighting, score regularization, recency correlation or optimization are adequate explanations. Half-cycle rotation preserves per-row correction-value histograms but does not perfectly remove temporal associations.

Query-by-prior interaction: action_target minus global_target is compared with action_context minus existing g2-r0001-context_separate. A benefit confined to target queries supports the conditional-relevance account; equal benefits imply generic count normalization. Historical context reference is identical in parameter construction and formula except bookkeeping, but remains a cross-round contrast.

At any checkpoint, diagnostics must show action counts and attention masses, correction changes for mixed histories, zero padded mass, norm agreement, and unchanged attention on single-action histories within floating precision. On equal-score synthetic histories the action mode must allocate 1/K mass to each of K present actions. These identities establish implementation behavior, not predictive utility.

Exploratory existing host slices: report all sample/positive/negative counts. Inspect behavior-present/absent and history-length slices; do not infer a count-imbalance effect from presence alone. Improvements in the large history_gt64 slice are consequential (3,026,583 impressions), while short-history and empty-history changes may reflect shared training and cannot show direct normalization effects.

Expected parameter count is the incumbent 17,130,275 with 51,587 dense parameters. Gather/scatter count bookkeeping adds O(BL) arithmetic and memory, not parameters. Measured training/inference time, allocated GPU cost and peak memory determine any efficiency conclusion.

Pre-host local checks completed: all four modules compile; only authorized numeric imports; module bodies differ only in literal CONFIG; inherited encoder/scorer/weight function ASTs and parameter-creating construction match the aligned ancestor. Independent scalar checks passed all 21,845 label sequences of length 0..7 for equal-score action mass, single-action invariance, count-histogram rotation and hierarchical-mixture equivalence. These are mathematical/source checks, not Torch execution or measured model performance; Torch is absent. No training was launched.
falsifiers: action_target fails to outperform matched global_target: this fixed full count correction is not a successful candidate; a single implementation failure does not refute all behavior-aware retrieval.
shifted_target matches or exceeds action_target: behavior-specific crowding explanation is not supported even if both improve.
Very few mixed or imbalanced supplied histories, negligible attention changes, or no reduction in frequent-behavior prior mass means the presumed bottleneck is weak or compensated by learned scores.
Nonfinite outputs, mask leakage, altered parameter shapes, or failed equal-score/single-action identities invalidate the implementation before a mechanism claim.
global_target differs materially from the historical exact replay: investigate source/recipe nondeterminism before attribution; do not treat an unexplained replay change as a new gain.
Seed reversals or user-cluster intervals crossing zero leave performance and attribution preliminary. A gain in one validation seed is insufficient for repeated support.
alternative_explanations: Action multiplicity may be useful interest-intensity evidence, consistent with DIN primary text; removing it can hurt. Full alpha=1 is intentionally a strong discriminating intervention rather than a tuned optimum.

Count correction changes gradient allocation and attention entropy; generic regularization rather than behavior semantics may explain improvement. Shifted correction controls the histogram, not every gradient trajectory or final entropy.

Behavior counts correlate with recency, user activity and category composition; half-cycle reassignment is a deterministic negative control and does not yield an exchangeable randomized causal estimate.
Only the last 128 supplied events are available, so measured counts do not represent all user activity. Static user/ad snapshot as-of dates remain undocumented under the frozen benchmark assumption.
Norm matching fixes per-example total magnitude but not component norms or directions; shared model training can change even empty-history predictions.
Adaptive validation reuse, best-checkpoint selection, one seed and candidate-supplied diagnostics on the first 512 impressions limit generality. No test or closed-assessment evidence is available.

cost_plan.stop_rule: Do not train in the coding jail. Host runs the registered variants. Stop on the declared hard global/per-trial limits, invalid information or ownership boundaries, or if a useful contrast plus assessment reserve no longer fits. Do not raise limits. Null results retain incumbent and are documented; no automatic retries with unknown execution state, no tuning on withheld outcomes.
